title: Bloom Algo
tagline: Bringing structure to the chaos of options trading.
summary: Automated options trading for retail buyers, kept transparent over WhatsApp.
disciplines: Product Strategy · Product Design · Visual Direction · Fintech
team: With the Bloom Algo product and engineering team
scope: Product direction, interaction model, visual language, design system

sections.heading: Options trading moves fast, but the way many retail traders approach it is still manual.
body: Too much monitoring. Too much emotion. Too many decisions happening in real time.
sections.statement: Bloom Algo was built to give retail option buyers a more structured way to participate, without needing to watch the market all day.

sections.heading: From reacting to executing
body: The product combines pre-built strategies, real-time execution, automated risk controls, and live WhatsApp alerts into one connected experience.
sections.statement: Let the system handle the execution. Keep the trader informed and in control.

sections.heading: Making complexity feel manageable
body: Algo trading can become intimidating very quickly.
The product needed to make sophisticated strategies feel approachable without hiding the underlying decisions.

Strategy selection, deployment, execution status, P&L, and risk events were organised around a clear visual hierarchy so traders could understand what was happening without constantly interpreting the interface.

sections.heading: Automation doesn't mean handing everything over.
body: Bloom Algo keeps the trader close to the action with live trade updates, strategy status, stop-loss events, and execution feedback delivered directly through WhatsApp.
The experience is designed around a simple relationship:

sections.heading: Designing the product language
body: The visual direction intentionally moves away from the aggressive, chart-heavy language common in trading products.
Soft gradients, a calm palette, rounded surfaces, and a more approachable visual language make a technically complex product feel less intimidating.
The challenge was finding the balance between:
sections.statement: Confidence and caution. Technology and humanity.

sections.heading: One system, many moments
body: From deploying a strategy to receiving an order confirmation, from a live P&L state to a stop-loss event, the experience had to remain coherent across different levels of urgency.
The product was designed as one connected system rather than a collection of trading screens.

sections.heading: Shaping the experience
body: I worked across the product direction, interaction model, visual language, and design system, translating a technically complex trading concept into a product experience that could be understood by retail traders.
The work involved making decisions about hierarchy, transparency, risk communication, and how much complexity to expose at each stage.

result.heading: The result
body: Bloom Algo turns a high-speed, high-complexity trading workflow into something more structured, visible, and manageable.
The product doesn't remove the risk of trading.
result.statement: It removes some of the unnecessary friction around it.
